title: Land Reforms & Green Revolution in India
summary: Land reforms restructured agrarian ownership through Zamindari abolition, while the Green Revolution boosted food grain yields via High Yielding Variety seeds.

blocks.title: First-Principles Core Truth
blocks.summary: Land reforms restructured agrarian ownership through Zamindari abolition, while the Green Revolution boosted food grain yields via High Yielding Variety seeds.

blocks.content: 1. Four Pillars of Land Reforms: Abolition of Intermediaries (Zamindari) | Tenancy Reform (Regulation of rent, security of tenure) | Land Ceiling Acts | Consolidation of Holdings.
2. First Constitutional Amendment (1951): Added 9th Schedule to protect land reform laws from judicial review under Fundamental Rights.
3. Green Revolution (Mid-1960s): Introduced High Yielding Variety (HYV) dwarf wheat seeds (Norman Borlaug & M.S. Swaminathan) + chemical fertilizers + controlled irrigation.
4. Regional Disparity Impact: First phase (1966-75) benefited Punjab, Haryana, and Western UP; second phase expanded to eastern states.

rows: 20 million tenants became direct landowners; ended feudal revenue extraction
Fixation of maximum rent (usually 1/4th to 1/5th of crop output)
Landowners used *Benami* transfers and loopholes to evade ceilings
Highly successful in Punjab & Haryana; neglected in eastern states

items: **HYV Seeds:** Semi-dwarf high-yielding wheat varieties (*Lerma Rojo, Sonora 64*) and rice (*IR-8*).
**Chemical Inputs:** Heavy application of Nitrogenous, Phosphatic, and Potassic (NPK) fertilizers.
**Assured Irrigation:** Canal network extension and tube-well electrification.
**Institutional Credit:** Expansion of Regional Rural Banks (RRBs 1975) and NABARD (1982).

blocks.content: ⚠️ **Exam Trap 1:** The 1st Constitutional Amendment (1951) created the **9th Schedule** specifically to protect early Zamindari Abolition Acts from court challenges.
⚠️ **Exam Trap 2:** Land ceiling reforms were most successful in **Kerala** and **West Bengal** (Operation Barga 1978), but largely failed across the rest of India due to legal loopholes.

#### Tier 1 — Recall MCQ
**Q:** Which Constitutional Amendment enacted in 1951 introduced the Ninth Schedule to protect state land reform legislation from judicial challenge?  
(A) First Amendment Act 1951  
(B) Forty-Second Amendment Act 1976  
(C) Forty-Fourth Amendment Act 1978  
(D) Seventy-Third Amendment Act 1992  
**Answer: — 1st Constitutional Amendment Act 1951 added the Ninth Schedule.

#### Tier 2 — Applied Scenario
**Scenario:** An agricultural policy report notes severe soil degradation, falling groundwater tables, and soil salinity in Punjab. Identify the historical technological roots.  
**Resolution:** Over-reliance on the Green Revolution package—unregulated tubewell pumping for water-intensive Paddy crops and imbalanced application of subsidized NPK fertilizers.

#### Tier 3 — Mains Descriptive Prompt
*'Evaluate the socio-economic impacts of land reforms in post-independent India. How did the Green Revolution transform national food security while creating regional disparities?'*
